title.narrative: Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance to the Most Vulnerable Communities in Aleppo and Al-Hasakeh

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed action will help the most vulnerable households (HHs) in two underserved sub-districts, As-Safira and Al-Hasakeh, access basic needs and reduce negative coping mechanisms. ACF and partners Al Ihsan (Aleppo) and Sanabel Al-Amal (Al-Hasakeh) will use proven experience in cash programming to distribute 6 rounds of MPCA to 450 HHs, reaching 2,250 individuals, while contributing more broadly to the wider communities, including markets. Based on needs assessments, community consultations and coordination with the CWG and Sector actors, in As-Safira ACF will target HHs of PwD, with specific priority given to single-headed HHs with PwD. In Al-Hasakeh sub-district, ACF will target HHs incurring catastrophic health-related expenditure due to chronic illness, with priority given to HHs with children diagnosed with cancer. ACF considered interventions implemented by other actors in the same sub-district, such as ongoing MPCA to HHs with PwD by UNICEF in Al-Hasakeh and will therefore focus on another most vulnerable group to avoid duplication and maximise impact for the whole sub-district. ACF uses a scoring system to prioritise the most vulnerable HHs. The action will be standardised and in accordance with Sector best practice, underpinned by localisation through collaboration with two implementing partners. Al Ihsan and Sanabel Al Amal will conduct HH assessments to confirm eligibility, collect data and verification documents, such as a disability ID or medical certificate issued by a hospital. The MPCA transfer value will correspond to CWG recommendations. ACF will monitor the MPCA, including on-site monitoring of distributions through spot checks, and a helpdesk to provide clarifications or address concerns during distribution. Post-Distribution Monitoring will be conducted to assess the impact and usage of MPCA. ACF will coordinate with DoSALs for effective implementation and partnership with NGOs, and to facilitate the needed approval from MoSAL and the Higher Relief Committee. ACF has full access to and capacity to operate in the targeted areas, as do both partners. To ensure synergy of efforts and avoid duplication, ACF is in coordination with the CWG, other cash actors, and DoSAL in the targeted locations. During proposal development, ACF coordinated with a range of INGOs intending to work in the same areas. This includes PUI and others as they intend to work in As-Safira (PUI’s planned MPCA intervention does not overlap with ACF, and ACF’s partner Al-Ihsan's planned food aid would be delivered in coordination with, but independently from this action). ACF and PUI are also in ongoing conversation about MPCA selection criteria to ensure not only that the interventions do not overlap, but that they can complement one another and allow for potential referrals where needed, collectively covering as much of the underserved sub-district as possible.ltbrgtACF will strengthen the capacity of both partners on protection and gender the action includes training on protection mainstreaming in MPCA, conveying essential practical information to assist LNGO staff in carefully considering and monitoring protection risks during implementation, while also avoiding exposing individuals to harm and ensuring equitable access to impartial assistance. The training aims to enhance knowledge of gender fundamentals, various forms of GBV, and their consequences. It also seeks to raise awareness among humanitarian workers about subconscious biases stemming from cultural influences and prejudices, which may unintentionally result in discrimination.ltbrgtLastly, ACF and both partners will ensure AAP through multiple communication channels, starting with community consultations, as a key factor in identifying targeted HHs, and dissemination of project information, particularly the MPCA eligibility criteria, within community groups. This will include mechanisms for beneficiaries to raise any concern with ACF.ltbrgtlt/pgt
